title: Shah Jahan Builds a Tomb for Mumtaz Mahal
text:
Arjumand Banu Begum married Prince Khurram, the future Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, in 1612. When he took the throne in 1628, she received the title Mumtaz Mahal, "chosen one of the palace." She was his constant companion and adviser, and traveled with him even on military campaigns, giving birth to fourteen children.

In 1631 she was with him on a campaign in the Deccan. In June, at Burhanpur, she gave birth to their fourteenth child, a daughter, and died soon afterwards. The court histories describe the emperor's grief as overwhelming: he went into mourning, gave up music and fine clothes for a time, and the whole court mourned with him.

Shah Jahan resolved to build her a tomb unlike any other. Her body was moved to Agra, and in the following years a white marble mausoleum rose on the bank of the Yamuna river, with gardens, a mosque and a guest house. Thousands of artisans and laborers worked on it, using marble from Makrana and stones from across Asia. The main tomb was finished around 1643 and the whole complex about ten years later.

Shah Jahan's last years were sad. In 1658 his son Aurangzeb seized the throne and confined him in the Agra fort, from which he could see the Taj Mahal across the river. When he died in 1666 he was buried beside her.
lesson: Grief for someone we love can be turned into something that lasts and gives beauty to others. Love is often measured best by what we build in its memory.
source: Abdul Hamid Lahori, Padshahnama; Ebba Koch, The Complete Taj Mahal (2006)
